discussion: The tests pass (CHK-0034). Now I need to add port documentation with doctest examples to Doc/library/urllib.parse.rst. The previous patch failed due to ambiguous old text (2 matches). I'll extend the old text to include the NFKC paragraph's first line to disambiguate, and insert the new explanation + doctest between the port paragraph and 'Unmatched square brackets'.

operation.new:
Reading the :attr:`port` attribute will raise a :exc:`ValueError` if
   an invalid port is specified in the URL.  See section
   :ref:`urlparse-result-object` for more information on the result object.

   The :attr:`port` attribute is validated only when it is accessed, not
   when the result object is constructed.  The port must be a decimal
   integer in the range 0 through 65535 (inclusive).  An absent or empty
   port component yields :const:`None`.  A port component that is not a
   valid decimal integer in range causes :attr:`port` to raise
   :exc:`ValueError`.

   .. doctest::

      >>> from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlparse
      >>> p = urlsplit('http://example.com:65536/')
      >>> p.netloc
      'example.com:65536'
      >>> p.port
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535
      >>> urlsplit('http://example.com:abc/').port
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'
      >>> urlsplit('http://example.com:0/').port
      0
      >>> urlsplit('http://example.com:65535/').port
      65535
      >>> urlparse('http://example.com:65536/').port
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535
      >>> urlparse('http://example.com:0/').port
      0

   Unmatched square brackets in the :attr:`netloc` attribute will raise a
   :exc:`ValueError`.

   Characters in the :attr:`netloc` attribute that decompose under NFKC
